chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman with whom her husband has intercourse, then she begins menstruating while she is in the bath place: should she perform ghusl or should she not perform ghusl? He said: “There has come upon her that which invalidates salat (prayer); she should not perform ghusl.”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمُغْتَسَلِ: the bathing place where ghusl is performed
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا: her husband has intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: If a woman begins menstruating after intercourse while about to perform ghusl, should she still do the ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who begins menstruating while preparing to perform ghusl after intercourse. The Imam عليه السلام states that since menstruation, which prevents salat (prayer), has commenced, she should not perform that ghusl at that time.
